hypotheses.justification: The statement `Function.Injective b` only needs X and b. [Fintype X] is taken as an argument only because it is instance-implicit and X is already an argument. The proof (b (b (b x)) = x gives b (b (b x)) = b (b (b y)) from b x = b y, so x = y) never uses finiteness, and the result holds for any type. It can be omitted with `omit [Fintype X] in`.

The statement and proof do not use decidable equality. The theorem is just injectivity of b, which follows from hb alone, so the instance is only auto-included as an instance-implicit variable over X. It can be omitted with `omit [DecidableEq X] in`. This is independent of [Fintype X].
